---
title: "Rebuild, cancel, delete"
description: "Manage a template over time: trigger new builds, cancel in-flight ones, delete stale templates"
---

## Rebuild

Queue a new build for an existing template, e.g. after a failed build, or to pick up an updated base image.

<CodeGroup>

```typescript TypeScript
const build = await template.rebuild()
console.log(`Build queued: ${build.id}`)
```

```python Python
build = template.rebuild()
print(f"Build queued: {build.id}")
```

</CodeGroup>

Rebuild is **idempotent**: if an in-flight build already exists with the same configuration, you get back the existing build instead of a duplicate.

To wait for the new build to finish, poll it by the ID that `rebuild()` returns. Continuing from the `build` above:

<CodeGroup>

```typescript TypeScript
let current = build
while (!["ready", "failed", "cancelled"].includes(current.status)) {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000))
  current = await template.getBuild(build.id)
}
console.log(current.status, current.errorMessage ?? "")
```

```python Python
import time

while build.status.value not in ("ready", "failed", "cancelled"):
    time.sleep(2)
    build = template.get_build(build.id)
print(build.status.value, build.error_message or "")
```

</CodeGroup>

<Note>
`rebuild()` does not update `latestBuildId` / `latest_build_id`. On a template returned by `Template.create`, `waitUntilReady()` / `wait_until_ready()` and `streamBuildLogs()` / `stream_build_logs()` keep following the first build. A template returned by `Template.connect` has no `latestBuildId`, so they follow the most recent build. Polling `getBuild()` / `get_build()` with the ID that `rebuild()` returns works in both cases.
</Note>

## List and inspect builds

`listBuilds()` / `list_builds()` returns the template's 20 most recent builds, newest first.

<CodeGroup>

```typescript TypeScript
const builds = await template.listBuilds()
for (const b of builds) {
  console.log(b.id, b.status, b.errorMessage ?? "")
}

const build = await template.getBuild(builds[0].id)
```

```python Python
builds = template.list_builds()
for b in builds:
    print(b.id, b.status.value, b.error_message or "")

build = template.get_build(builds[0].id)
```

</CodeGroup>

## Cancel an in-flight build

<CodeGroup>

```typescript TypeScript
await template.cancelBuild(build.id)
```

```python Python
template.cancel_build(build.id)
```

</CodeGroup>

`cancelBuild` is a no-op for builds already in a terminal state.

## Delete a template

<CodeGroup>

```typescript TypeScript
await template.delete()

// Or by UUID
await Template.deleteById("7a3f2b8c-1234-...")
```

```python Python
template.delete()

# Or by UUID
Template.delete_by_id("7a3f2b8c-1234-...")
```

</CodeGroup>

Both calls are idempotent on `404`. Once the delete succeeds the template's `name` is released for reuse — you can immediately create a new template with the same name.

A template can't be deleted while something still uses it:

- a sandbox created from the template that is not deleted, including a paused one
- a snapshot of such a sandbox, even after the sandbox itself is deleted

The call then raises `ConflictError` with a message such as `template has 2 sandbox(es) or snapshot(s) still referencing it; delete them first`. Kill the sandboxes and delete their snapshots, then delete the template again. `Snapshot.list()` lists the snapshots of one sandbox, so keep the IDs of the sandboxes you create from a template:

<CodeGroup>

```typescript TypeScript
import { Sandbox, Snapshot } from "@superserve/sdk"

// sandboxIds: the sandboxes you created from this template
for (const sandboxId of sandboxIds) {
  await Sandbox.killById(sandboxId)
  for (const snapshot of await Snapshot.list(sandboxId)) {
    await Snapshot.deleteById(snapshot.id)
  }
}
await template.delete()
```

```python Python
from superserve import Sandbox, Snapshot

# sandbox_ids: the sandboxes you created from this template
for sandbox_id in sandbox_ids:
    Sandbox.kill_by_id(sandbox_id)
    for snapshot in Snapshot.list(sandbox_id):
        Snapshot.delete_by_id(snapshot.id)
template.delete()
```

</CodeGroup>
